subject: Greenfield connectivity decision: VPC peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S VPN
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Subject: Greenfield connectivity decision: quick read + ask

Team—

EdgeWave (contact: Tom Reynolds, network-ops@edgewave.ai) is signing up for a private deployment (VPC + dedicated pool) and has asked us to recommend a connectivity pattern. Their constraints:
- Primary region: us-west-2, will expand to eu-west-1 in 2027
- Strict egress controls (no direct public IPs for inference servers)
- Expect sustained 2500 rps across traffic spikes; p95 latency SLO 120ms
- Compliance: SOC2 + healthcare integrations (so auditability and private peering are important)

They asked us to evaluate VPC peering, PrivateLink (interface endpoints), and site-to-site (S2S) VPN for their greenfield deployment. I sketched three tradeoffs (attached: edgewave-network-diagram-v2.pdf). Can you each give a short recommendation and ops notes (HA, BGP, MTU, route propagation, billing impact, cross-region implications)?

Aim: short internal memo by EOD PST so we can include it in the SOW draft.

Thanks—
Hannah

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Greenfield connectivity decision: quick read + ask

+1 on PrivateLink as the primary recommendation for EdgeWave. Quick notes:
- Security: PrivateLink keeps traffic on the cloud provider fabric and avoids having to route customer subnets into our VPC. That maps well to their no-public-IP egress requirement.
- Ownership: Endpoint services are owned by us; we will publish an interface endpoint service in us-west-2. That gives them strong control over access via endpoint policies.
- HA/Scaling: Recommend two AZ-spread N LB frontends plus multiple endpoint ENIs. Test endpoint scale — expect per-endpoint bandwidth limits (cloud provider throttles) so we should provide guidance on multiple endpoints per region.
- Cost: Interface endpoints + NLB + data processed charges can be higher than peering at scale; we'll capture numbers in the attached privatelink-cost-estimate.xlsx.
- Ops: Endpoint certificate rotation (if we do mTLS termination) and endpoint policy governance (tight allow lists) are key operational tasks.

My call: PrivateLink primary; S2S VPN for DR if they want an on-prem fallback, but S2S alone won't meet p95 SLAs for latency-sensitive traffic.

Marissa

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T11:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Greenfield connectivity decision: quick read + ask

Agree with Marissa but adding the network engineering caveats:
- VPC peering: Good for low-cost high-throughput intra-region traffic and preserves source IP with proper route tables. Caveats: no transitive peering (will complicate multi-region expansion), and peering across accounts requires explicit routes. It also means our VPC route table grows (scale) and we need to manage overlapping CIDRs carefully.
- PrivateLink: avoids route table explosion and supports per-service IAM/policy controls. MTU: interface endpoints typically reduce MTU (e.g., 1500 -> 1436 depending on cloud), so we should check packet size for gRPC + protobuf bundles; enable TCP MSS clamping on their edge routers if necessary.
- S2S VPN: fine as a supplemental path for bursty batch traffic or admin plane; for production inference traffic it's risky unless they have managed SD-WAN with predictable latencies. Use BGP with two tunnels/paths for redundancy and active/passive failover, and monitor for asymmetric routing.

Operational recommendations:
- Multi-AZ endpoints, monitor ENI saturation and per-minute packets.
- Pre-authorize our service consumer VPCs in a documented workflow (avoid last-minute CIDR swaps).
- For cross-region (us-west-2 -> eu-west-1), run regional PrivateLink endpoints + controlled routing (avoid cross-region peering).

Marcus
Senior Solutions Architect

Thanks for the quick notes — helpful. A couple clarifying items from our side:
- Our current on-prem stack terminates TLS at a perimeter proxy; we can do mTLS to Redwood if needed.
- We have an MPLS-backed SD-WAN that gives us decent latency (~30–40ms to us-west-2) and predictable jitter; we can bring up BGP.
- We are sensitive to per-GB charges; our finance team will push back on high egress-like costs even for private-link data charges.
- We want one canonical path for low-latency inference calls; DR path is acceptable to be slower/batch oriented.

Can you send a short recommendation we can include in our infra runbook and also the SOW draft? If PrivateLink is your primary rec, list the operational playbook (LB sizing guidance, endpoint counts per AZ, failover behavior) and an order-of-magnitude cost delta vs peering.

Thanks—

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@edgewave.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: network-ops@edgewave.ai
Date: 2026-11-30T08:50:00-08:00
Subject: Recommendation: Primary PrivateLink + S2S VPN DR (summary & attachments)

Tom / EdgeWave team —

Summary recommendation (short):
- Primary connectivity: PrivateLink (interface endpoint service) in us-west-2. Rationale: private cloud fabric, strong access controls, avoids exposing customer subnets to our VPC routing. Matches your egress-control requirement and simplifies audit trails for SOC2.
- DR/fallback: Managed S2S VPN over your SD-WAN with BGP. Purpose: control plane and bulk/batch traffic only; not the primary low-latency path.
- Peering: Not recommended as the primary for greenfield multi-account/private deployments because of transitive limitations and route table management overhead. Acceptable only if EdgeWave wants very high throughput intra-region and can commit to CIDR/route hygiene.

Operational playbook (high-level):
1) Endpoint sizing: start with 2 NLBs (public/internal as appropriate) across 3 AZs. Recommend 4 interface endpoints provisioned (2 per AZ pair) as an initial baseline. For 2500 rps (inference payloads ~1–2KB), estimate 400–600 Mbps sustained; plan for 3x headroom for spikes.
2) HA: AZ-spread NLBs + endpoint ENIs in each AZ, two redundant endpoints per AZ. Health checks at 10s, aggressive failover for backend pool.
3) MTU/TCP: verify MSS clamping; add TCP window tuning where necessary.
4) Policy: endpoint service policy whitelists only EdgeWave consumer VPC(s); require mTLS for client-auth when invoking inference endpoints.
5) Monitoring & alerts: ENI utilization, NLB active connections, TLS error rate, p95 latency per region. Instrument with our tracing headers so we can correlate across customer calls.
6) Cost hedge: enable a low-latency trial for 2 weeks and track egress-equivalent charges; during SOW we include a one-time credit to offset onboarding spike.

I've attached: edgewave-network-diagram-v2.pdf (updated topology), privatelink-cost-estimate.xlsx (order-of-magnitude), sow-draft-edgewave.docx (language for the SOW including a DR appendix).

Next steps:
- Tom: confirm you want PrivateLink primary + S2S for DR and whether you want us to size the NLBs to support 2x or 3x burst capacity.
- Marissa/Marcus: I'll include your technical notes in the SOW; Marcus please add the MTU/MSS paragraph to INF-7842.

Hannah
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
